text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 index finished at a record for the eight consecutive session despite a wave of profit-taking on Wall Street. The leading blue chip index, up for the 11th straight session, added 21.4 points to close at 4,691.0, as advancers beat decliners by a margin of two to one.

FRANKFURT - The German stock market regained momentum and the DAX index ended at a record closing level. The DAX index closed up 19.78 points at 3,595.15. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,559.29 down 33.85.

PARIS - French stocks closed with a big gain, but remained below an all-time high. Stocks were boosted by a strong gain on Wall Street on Monday and on new opinion polls showing a lead for the ruling centre-right majority. The CAC-40 index closed up 26.49 points or 0.98 percent at 2,719.58.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended narrowly off the intra-day high, but were still able to post a second closing high. Foreign buying, a recovery in the dollar and Wall Street's overnight gains were the main reasons behind the rise, dealers said. The All share SPI index closed up 25.39 points at 3,212.87.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed mixed. Steadiness in the yen-dollar exchange rate initially stimulated buying in major high-tech shares such as Sony Corp., but the buying momentum ran out of steam later. The 225-share Nikkei average ended 14.40 points lower or 0.07 percent at 20,129.11.

HONG KONG - After nine consecutive winning sessions, Hong Kong share prices finally gave up some ground, ending weaker as stocks ran into profit-taking and the Hang Seng Index met resistance above 14,000 points. The index fell 81.34 points, or 0.58 percent, to close at 13,906.46.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock rose to a record close, taking its cue from another record run on Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index added 9.5 points to close at 2,534.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares edged slightly higher amid late rises in the bullion price, spurred by some dollar weakness. Bullion was last bid at $348.20 an ounce. The Gold index ended up 7.6 points at 1,275.4, Industrials down 1.4 points to 8,474.7, and the all-share index up 2.8 points to 7,193.1.
